Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team needs to confirm the transfer mechanism and understand what evidence Redwood can provide so we can close our procurement window. Two asks:

1) Which SCCs module(s) do you recommend for a standard SaaS inference integration where Redwood acts as a processor for model inference and is permitted to engage subprocessors (cloud infra)? We are in the UK but have EU users and want a single approach that covers both jurisdictions.

2) Can you share a timeline for delivering the SOC2/HIPAA evidence excerpts we requested, plus a completed SIG/CAIQ snapshot and the basic DPIA notes? Our procurement target is end of November.

Attachments: Oxbridge-SIG-questions-v2.xlsx

Appreciate a short runbook/plan we can include on our side.

Best,

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and a proposed delivery plan.

1) SCCs module recommendation: our legal and privacy teams generally recommend executing the EU SCCs with the UK Addendum where required, and applying Module Two (processor-to-controller) in combination with a UK Addendum for UK-resident data. For simplicity across EU + UK we often standardize on the EU SCCs (controller-processor) plus the UK Addendum, with an annex listing subprocessors and permitted subprocess operations.

2) Evidence timeline (proposed):
- Today (Nov 10): confirm scope and list of specific SIG/CAIQ rows Oxbridge needs prioritized.
- Nov 12: Redwood provides a curated evidence package: SOC2 report excerpts (controls matrix redacted as needed), HIPAA attestation summary, SIG baseline PDF, and the DPA/draft SCCs for review.
- Nov 15: Finalized SCCs + UK Addendum and completed evidence checklist (we aim for this; DocuSign to follow).

Assignees: Marissa will coordinate evidence artifacts, Laura will confirm module selection and final clause language with legal. I will sync with your LegalOps to get any redlines into a single DocuSign flow.

Are you available for a 30-minute alignment call on Nov 11 at 09:00 UTC? If so, I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: EU/UK transfers — SCCs module preference and evidence request

Quick legal note on the module selection and a drafting point: 

- Module choice: because Oxbridge is a controller and Redwood will operate as a processor that may engage cloud subprocessors, the EU SCCs (controller-processor) with the UK Addendum is the pragmatic path. There is a secondary approach (processor-to-processor flow using Module Three) if Oxbridge insists on a P2P architecture, but that is atypical for our SaaS inference offering.
- Annexes: ensure we include a subprocessors annex (name, location, purpose) and a short technical/security annex that references our SOC2 scope, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and data retention limits.
- Clause redlines to flag: data subject rights response time, audit access window (we cap on-site audits; remote evidence is the primary route), and subprocessors notification timeframe.

I will draft the SCCs + UK Addendum language and share a tracked draft by Nov 15. If procurement asks for an executed UK addendum first, we can accommodate with a targeted DocuSign flow limited to the UK Addendum plus a side letter covering subprocessors.

– Laura
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
